review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. ODFW and NOAA sources support rocky reef habitat and broad depth use; thermal evidence is regional/life-stage limited, not a validated SST preference curve.

profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for copper rockfish.
factors.value_notes: A NOAA Puget Sound status review and a young-of-year thermal-performance study provide regional and early-life evidence: copper rockfish environmental temperatures in the Puget Sound account are about 7-13 °C, and recruit foraging/growth/survival respond to warming. These sources do not establish adult preferred satellite SST or validate the configured 8-16 °C range and 10-14 °C ideal across the species' range.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for copper rockfish.
factors.value_notes: ODFW describes copper rockfish as a common shallow rocky-water species and reports occurrence to 100 fathoms; NOAA documents adults on rocky reefs and rock-sand bottoms, with strong regional depth variation (generally deeper in southern California and shallower in British Columbia). This supports broad depth/habitat association but does not validate one 5-100 m / 7-95 m ideal across regions and life stages.
